Textile: Second Temple parokhet · Mishnah weave specification
Use/Location: Curtain system separating Holy Place and Holy of Holies
Thickness: 1 handbreadth; derived working conversion 0.0875m if 1 cubit=6 handbreadths. Keep conversion as working-model value, not archaeological measurement.
Material/Fiber: Fine linen + blue wool + purple wool + scarlet wool
Color/Dye: Blue / purple / scarlet / fine-linen natural-light component; exact dye chemistry and modern RGB unresolved
Weave/Yarn Structure: Traditional record: 72 composite yarn/cord units; each composite unit has 24 threads, interpreted as 6 threads of each of the four material/color components. Treat as yarn-construction evidence, not as literal total warp-count across entire curtain.
Pattern/Embroidery: Mishnah entry defines weave/material, not exact figured motif. Motif comes from Josephus variant and must remain separate.
Edge/Seam/Hanging: Exact selvedge, loom width, seams, suspension rings/beam and lower weighting unresolved; require reconstruction variants.
Drape/Weight Rule: Extremely massive/heavy ceremonial textile tradition; 300-priest immersion language indicates exceptional bulk, but do not derive kilograms from this alone.
Shader Contract: Four fiber/material masks; visible weave at close range; no velvet/satin look. Thickness should create believable edge cross-section and folds.
Blender Cloth Contract: Model macro thickness as real solid/cloth shell, not single-sided plane. Cloth simulation uses tuned mass/bending to reproduce heavy hanging; simulation parameters are implementation values, not historical measurements. Use separate warp/weft normals and fiber fuzz.
Notes: Two curtains per year are mentioned in the tradition; exact production interpretation has textual variants.
